hello.note: For anyone. More respectful, to an older person: ጤና ይስጥልኝ (TE-na yis-TIL-lign), may God give you health

how-are-you.note: The polite form, the same whoever you ask. Between friends it changes: እንዴት ነህ (neh) to a man, እንዴት ነሽ (nesh) to a woman

im-well.note: The same for a man or a woman. Many people answer እግዚአብሔር ይመስገን (ig-zee-AB-heer yi-mes-GEN), thanks be to God

good-morning.note: Literally "how did you pass the night?", the polite form

good-night.note: Literally "pass the night well", the polite form

goodbye.note: Literally "be well", the polite form. Friends say ቻው (chaw), from Italian ciao

please.note: The polite form, the same whoever you ask

thank-you.note: በጣም አመሰግናለሁ (be-TAM ...) means thank you very much

yes.note: A quick intake of breath, like a little gasp, also means yes

no.note: አይ፣ አመሰግናለሁ (ay, a-me-se-gi-NAL-lo) is no, thank you

excuse-me.note: Sorry, and excuse me to get attention or get past

my-name.note: The name goes in the middle: the verb comes last. The audio uses Peter as the example name

your-name.note: The polite form, the same whoever you ask

where-from.note: Answer ከ... ነኝ (ke ... negn), I'm from...

dont-understand.note: Literally "it didn't enter me", the same for a man or a woman

speak-english.note: English is taught in schools; many young people in Addis Ababa speak it

would-like.note: Literally "please give me ...", the polite way to order, the same for a man or a woman. The audio uses ቡና (BU-na), coffee

i-want.note: "I want ...", the thing first. The audio uses ይሄንን (yi-HEN-nin), this one

do-you-have.note: Literally "is there ...?" The audio uses ውሃ (wu-HA), water

just-looking.note: The same for a man or a woman

discount.note: Literally "will you lower it for me?" Bargaining is normal in markets such as Addis Ababa's Merkato

card.note: Big hotels take cards. Elsewhere it's cash or phone payments, so carry birr

checkout-time.note: Check whether a time is Ethiopian time: the day's hours start at 6 am, so 7 o'clock in the morning is 1 o'clock

taxi.note: Literally "will you call me a taxi?" Blue-and-white minibus taxis follow fixed routes; ride apps such as Ride work in Addis Ababa

train.note: The railway runs from Addis Ababa to Djibouti

bus.note: Long-distance buses leave very early, often before dawn

which-train.note: ወደ (we-DE) means to. The audio uses ጅቡቲ (ji-BU-tee), Djibouti, as the example
which-train.spoken: ወደ ጅቡቲ የሚሄደው ባቡር የትኛው ነው?

two-tickets.note: The audio uses ባሕር ዳር (ba-HIR DAR), Bahir Dar, as the example
two-tickets.spoken: ወደ ባሕር ዳር ሁለት ትኬት፣ እባክዎ

trip-length.note: Literally "to ..., how many hours does it take?" The audio uses Bahir Dar
trip-length.spoken: ወደ ባሕር ዳር ስንት ሰዓት ይወስዳል?

delicious.note: Ethiopian food is eaten with the right hand, tearing off injera, the spongy flatbread

allergic.note: Literally "... doesn't agree with me", the same for a man or a woman. The food goes first: ኦቾሎኒ (o-cho-LO-nee) peanuts, ዓሣ (a-SA) fish, እንቁላል (in-k'u-LAL) eggs. The audio uses peanuts

vegetarian.note: Literally "I don't eat meat", the same for a man or a woman

vegan.note: Fasting food, with no meat, eggs, or milk: vegan, and served everywhere on Wednesdays and Fridays

love-dish.note: Literally "I liked this food very much"

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.note: For more people: ለሶስት (le-SOST), 3, or ለአራት (le-a-RAT), 4

recommend.note: On Wednesdays, Fridays, and during fasts, many dishes are vegan (ፆም, tsom)

beer.note: Local beers include St. George and Habesha. Try ጠጅ (t'ej), honey wine

coffee.note: Ethiopia is coffee's homeland. Being invited to a coffee ceremony, three rounds roasted and brewed in front of you, is an honor

tea.note: Often spiced, with cinnamon or cloves

chicken.note: Doro wat, spicy chicken stew, is the national dish

hot.note: Hot to touch, and also fresh. Spicy is ያቃጥላል (ya-k'a-t'i-LAL), it burns

help.note: Shout it. The police are on 991

leave-me-alone.note: To a man. To a woman, ተዪኝ (te-YIGN)

need-doctor.note: The same for a man or a woman. For an ambulance, call 907

pharmacy.note: Also መድኃኒት ቤት (med-ha-NEET bet), the medicine house
